content.rationale:
Three prerequisites meet in one reading: the reconcile requirement reports the open records whose workspace jj lacks and changes nothing (yozqornv), the `deccy drafts` requirement lists every record with its state, the workspace it names and the same drift answer per record (qspsyqlp), and the record's shape, states and references are already a Quint model, `specs/drafts/state.qnt` (tvtnokzu). Both requirement sentences are one reading of one registry against one set of facts — the workspaces jj has — so one module carries them: `specs/drafts/drift.qnt` imports `draft_state` and restates none of the record, in the form the house uses for a reading (`specs/store_bulk/read.qnt`) and for a module that steps only the registry variable `records` (`specs/drafts/guard.qnt`).

The reading adds no registry state, and the module has no variable of its own. `draft_state` holds exactly one variable, `records`, and a record's fields are exactly the six the document fixes (tvtnokzu); existence is not one of them, because jj owns whether a workspace exists and the registry's naming of one is a reference, not custody (yozqornv, through xkolyytz). Existence therefore enters each reading as an input — the workspaces jj has, asked of jj — rather than as a second variable or a seventh field, and the report is derived from `records` and that input at each invocation rather than stored: no report field is added to `Record`, no report variable is added to the module, and no workspace is modelled at all. Putting either in the registry would hand the artifact a fact the prerequisites place elsewhere: existence with jj, meaning with the record.

The input is a predicate, not a set of paths. `missing(ws, jjHas)` asks `jjHas: (Workspace) => bool`, which holds of the workspaces jj has and is supplied to the reading; `drift` combines it with the record. A set of workspace paths (or any concrete key) would fix how a record's name and path are matched to a jj workspace, and that match is expressly left open by nzrnrlky, which qspsyqlp takes as a prerequisite; the predicate carries existence as jj's answer and fixes no matching rule of its own. Nor can existence be read off the registry: an open record whose workspace is gone is possible only because nothing in the registry can make jj keep a workspace (yozqornv), so the module never derives `jjHas` from `records`.

`drift(r, jjHas)` is `r.state == Open` and the named workspace missing. The state alone decides whether an absence counts: `open` is the record of a draft that has not landed and a draft is written in its own workspace, so a vanished workspace under an open record is drift; `landed` is the record of a draft that has landed, so the same absence is the normal end of a draft and is not drift, and a workspace jj still has for a landed record is not drift either (yozqornv, through vuopwuyo and vkkwusty; tvtnokzu's `State`). The determination is one boolean per record — no third state, category or outcome, because the record form has two values and the reading asks one question.

`Report` is the per-record row: the handle the record is filed under, its state, the workspace it names, and the drift flag. That is exactly what each requirement reports — the listing's handle, state and workspace (qspsyqlp, kwqnrzoz), and the answer to whether that workspace is missing while the record still asserts a draft (qspsyqlp, yozqornv). The record's node, edit and base are not in the row: the listing lists records and never nodes or edits (nzrnrlky), and nothing about ordering, counting or presentation is fixed, because the prerequisites leave it open (vuopwuyo, twpvqstu).

`listing(jjHas)` is the registry's keys mapped to their reports: every record once, under the handle that keys it, landed records included — landing removes no record and the directory's contents are the whole scan (qspsyqlp, twpvqstu), and the flag is answered per row rather than summarised. `reconcile(jjHas)` is the same report map restricted to the records `drift` holds of, keyed by handle; a landed record is retained in the registry and merely absent from the report, which is not dropping it (yozqornv, vkkwusty). It is built by inserting each kept record's entry into the accumulator: the write is an insert (`put`, which inserts an absent key), not an assignment at an existing key (`set`, which raises when the key is absent), so a non-empty report is reachable - yozqornv's reconcile report, which the gate's amended fact checks (nlquzopu). Because the keys are the registry's distinct handles, each write inserts and none replaces, so the fold's order cannot show.

The reading is a read in the model as in the requirements: `reconcileRead` and `listingRead` are the module's two steps, and each sets `records' = records`, so no record is added, removed or rewritten, no state moves, and — the module holding no workspace — none is created or removed; a drifted record stays open and still names the workspace it names, which is what the report is about (yozqornv, qspsyqlp, vuopwuyo). The two steps differ in what they report, not in what they change, and `step` says that nothing else is a step of this module. Deliberately not modelled: the verb's spelling, output form and exit status, the scan of `.deccy/work/`, the jj invocation that answers `jjHas` and its matching, ordering or counts, and any repair — the prerequisites place each of those outside this reading.
